questions.prompt: Two chemically linked steps at matched conditions have ΔG values+20.0 kJ and−35.0 kJ for the coupled amounts. What is the net free-energy change?
questions.explanation: A is correct. Free-energy changes add for the linked net process:20.0−35.0=−15.0. B is incorrect: that adds magnitudes rather than signed changes. C is incorrect: that reverses the net sign. D is incorrect: that omits the unfavorable step.

questions.prompt: A designed coupled mechanism links one+50 kJ transformation to three occurrences of a−20 kJ driving step. What is the net free-energy change for that linked cycle?
questions.explanation: C is correct. The driver contribution is3(−20)=−60 kJ, so the sum is50−60=−10. A is incorrect: that includes only one driving occurrence. B is incorrect: that does not use the specified stoichiometric combination. D is incorrect: that adds the driver magnitude with the wrong sign.

questions.prompt: Supplied linked steps are A+C→I+X, ΔG=+25 kJ, and I→B, ΔG=−40 kJ. Which net equation and value result?
questions.explanation: D is correct. The common intermediate I cancels, and signed free energies add. A is incorrect: I is both produced and consumed and cancels from the net equation. B is incorrect: the signs must be retained. C is incorrect: reversing the net equation also reverses its free-energy sign.

questions.prompt: For a supplied matched set of conditions, an uphill biosynthetic step has ΔG=+18.0 kJ per cycle and a linked ATP-hydrolysis step has ΔG=−30.5 kJ per cycle. What is the linked net change?
questions.explanation: B is correct. The mechanism-coupled sum is18.0−30.5=−12.5 under the supplied conditions. A is incorrect: that adds magnitudes. C is incorrect: that omits the synthesis cost. D is incorrect: that reverses the net sign.

questions.prompt: How can an electrolytic apparatus drive a redox process that is thermodynamically unfavorable in the intended direction?
options: A wire alone makes every reaction favorable
The negative ΔG of the isolated chemical process changes sign merely because electrodes are named
An external electrical source supplies energy to the process.
A salt bridge creates unlimited chemical energy
questions.explanation: C is correct. The powered overall system can drive a chemical change that would not operate as a self-powered cell in that direction. A is incorrect: a conductor is not an energy source. B is incorrect: the chemical direction remains uphill; external work drives it. D is incorrect: a bridge supports ionic charge balance rather than supplying energy.

questions.prompt: Light can drive an overall photosynthetic conversion that would be unfavorable without an energy input. What role does light play?
options: It supplies external energy coupled to chemical transformations.
It is only a catalyst and supplies no energy
It guarantees the isolated dark reaction has negative ΔG
questions.explanation: A is correct. Photon energy can support uphill chemical storage through an appropriate reaction pathway. B is incorrect: absorbed light can deliver energy. C is incorrect: the energy input is part of the overall accounting. D is incorrect: external driving does not prove that the unpowered reaction is favorable.

questions.prompt: Why does simply placing an unrelated exergonic reaction beside an endergonic reaction not necessarily drive the latter?
options: The two ΔG values can never be added even for a genuinely linked net process
An effective chemical or energetic coupling pathway is required.
Every exergonic reaction stops when any endergonic reactant is nearby
Endergonic processes violate thermodynamics under every possible external drive
questions.explanation: B is correct. Free energy released into an unrelated route may dissipate rather than be transferred to the desired transformation. A is incorrect: they can be added when the equations and amounts form the intended coupled process. C is incorrect: mere proximity does not impose that rule. D is incorrect: coupling or external energy can make them occur.

questions.prompt: A target step has ΔG=+15 kJ. A proposed driver has ΔG=−25 kJ in its forward direction, but the proposed linkage actually requires that driver in reverse. What is the net ΔG for one occurrence of each?
questions.explanation: D is correct. The reversed driver costs+25 kJ, so the sum is15+25=40 kJ. A is incorrect: that uses the driver in the wrong direction. B is incorrect: that incorrectly negates both uphill contributions. C is incorrect: that subtracts magnitudes despite both linked steps being uphill.

questions.prompt: For two genuinely coupled steps in fixed matching amounts, one uphill and one downhill, when is their overall process favorable under the specified conditions?
options: Whenever either step is downhill, regardless of magnitude
When the magnitude of the negative contribution exceeds the positive contribution.
Only when each individual step is downhill
Whenever a catalyst is added, regardless of the sum
questions.explanation: B is correct. Their signed sum must be negative. A is incorrect: a small favorable contribution may not offset a larger cost. C is incorrect: an uphill step can be supported by a sufficiently favorable linked step. D is incorrect: catalysis does not replace the net free-energy requirement.

questions.prompt: An ideal designed cycle can couple one−55 kJ driving event to an integer number of+20 kJ target events. What is the largest number of target events that still gives a negative total ΔG?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Two cost40 kJ, giving−15 kJ net; three cost60 kJ, giving+5 kJ and no longer a negative total. A is incorrect: one is feasible, but two also retain a negative sum. B is incorrect: the resulting+5 kJ is not favorable. D is incorrect: the finite driver energy limits how many uphill events it can offset.

questions.prompt: A power supply is disconnected after driving an uphill chemical conversion. Which statement avoids confusing thermodynamic driving with subsequent kinetics?
options: The external drive is gone, but the produced material may persist if its reverse transformation is kinetically slow.
The material must instantly reverse because the power was removed
The material proves the unpowered forward reaction became permanently favorable
A catalyst must now supply the same energy indefinitely
questions.explanation: A is correct. Removing the energy source does not require immediate chemical reversal; barriers still affect the time scale. B is incorrect: thermodynamics alone does not set an instantaneous rate. C is incorrect: externally driven formation does not establish that claim. D is incorrect: a catalyst is not an energy source.
